what: Random control (Table 1) = each agent casts a uniformly random one-hot letter vote; D(q) computed with the paper's composite
why: Paper only says 'random-uniform scoring control'. Of three readings tested (one-hot votes: mean D 0.730; uniform letter + uniform confidence: 0.556; Dirichlet(1) distributions: 0.494) only one-hot votes reproduce the paper's mean D 0.732.

what: Static rows: inference is deterministic, so for n=300 (= whole test split) all seeds see the same questions; n=50 rows use a seeded 50-question subsample of the test split per seed
why: Paper reports mean +/- sd over seeds 42/1337/2024 for static runs without saying what the seed varies; subsampling is the only seed-dependent part of a deterministic static evaluation.
